affected_system: pedestrian right-of-way, crossings, sidewalks, and accessible routes
alternatives: compare eligible treated and credible untreated units for phased quick-build pedestrian safety treatment
estimate pre-specified overall and distributional effects of phased quick-build pedestrian safety treatment
pair matched corridor event-study with exposure measurement with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Crash, conflict, barrier, sidewalk, crossing, and demand data have explicit observation processes.
Accessibility is evaluated across route continuity, slope, surface, crossing, and obstruction dimensions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain pre-intervention conditions for phased quick-build pedestrian safety treatment.

constraints.description: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: vision-zero director and accessibility compliance officer
decision_question: Did phased quick-build treatments reduce measured conflicts and improve accessible crossing performance?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for phased quick-build pedestrian safety treatment passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: matched corridor event-study with exposure measurement
independence_key.primary_outcome: change in exposure-normalized severe pedestrian conflicts

intended_claim: A versioned evaluate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting phased quick-build pedestrian safety treatment, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: change in exposure-normalized severe pedestrian conflicts
distributional gap in change in exposure-normalized severe pedestrian conflicts
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer injury prevention from unvalidated conflict detection or uncontrolled before-after counts.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for phased quick-build pedestrian safety treatment passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.

title: Evaluate quick-build pedestrian safety treatments
transportability_risks: Street design, enforcement, mobility-device needs, exposure, and reporting vary by place.
Crash-only models underrepresent near misses and unreported accessibility barriers.
